articles.title: Council Votes on Pet Adoption Fair After Long Debate
articles.deck: Residents of Upper Commons filled the hall on Friday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 5 weeks once it begins. Sadie Jurgens, who has lived in Upper Commons for 5 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The Upper Commons Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.
The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for pet adoption fair along Kiln Place, with work expected to start in September.

body: Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings. Simone Underhill, who has lived on Yardley Terrace for 15 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at Millrace Green on Friday at 7 p.m. The effort began in June when a handful of neighbors met at Millrace Green to talk about free tax clinic.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Millrace Library Branch
body: To the editor: I have lived on Harbor Court for 39 years, and I want to say what a difference the Millrace Library branch has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the June meeting.
Please keep the pet adoption fair in the budget. Many of us on Harbor Court use it every week.
Janet Chandler, Upper Commons

articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
